newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi takes EMU dig at EU partners.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi takes EMU dig at EU partners.

text.p: Italy's fitness for Europe's planned single currency must be judged on its own merits and not depend on domestic political considerations in other EU countries, Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Friday.

"I want to be clear. Being inside or outside Europe must be the result of our actions. We want to be judged on them," Prodi told a congress of the centrist Popular Party, a partner in his centre-left coalition.
"The judgement on Italy cannot depend on what suits domestic policy in other European countries, however big they are," Prodi said.

He did not elaborate but the remarks again signalled Italian sensitivity that some of its EU partners, including Germany, would prefer Italy not to be a founder member of the planned union in 1999 because lira involvement would weaken the new euro currency.

Prodi has pushed through a tough 1997 budget, with 62.5 trillion lire of deficit cuts including an unpopular one-off "Euro tax" levy, to try to ensure that Italy's deficit/GDP ratio is within the limits set down for membership of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
Prodi told the congress the government would not hesitate to draw up a supplementary budget in the coming months if necessary to keep Italy's EMU hopes alive.
